title: Gray Code Converter
constraints: Both converters are 8 bits wide and work independently.
Purely combinational: no flip-flops or latches.
hints: Binary → Gray: each Gray bit is the XOR of a binary bit and the bit above it, i.e. `bin ^ (bin >> 1)`.
Gray → binary: the MSB is copied, then `bin_out[i] = bin_out[i+1] ^ gray_in[i]` going down.
Equivalently, `bin_out[i]` is the XOR-reduction of all Gray bits from position `i` upward: `^(gray_in >> i)`.
